target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures describe the revenue sources for the Asset & Wealth Management segment (management fees, incentive fees, private banking/lending, and investments) and the recognition criteria for incentive fees. The 2025 disclosure D108 provides the updated narrative and figures for the current year, directly corresponding to the 2024 D090 structure and content.

Disclosure D096 (2024) specifically details the recognition of incentive fees and the amount of unrecognized incentive fees ($4.12B). Disclosure D108 (2025) contains the corresponding section on incentive fee recognition and the updated unrecognized incentive fees amount ($5.24B). These are matched within the broader D108 disclosure which covers the segment revenue overview including incentives.

current_disclosures.summary: Asset & Wealth Management generates revenues from management and other fees (primarily asset-based), incentive fees (including overrides based on performance benchmarks), private banking and lending (net interest income from loans and deposits), and investments related to asset management activities. sentences.text: • Management and other fees. We receive fees related to managing assets for institutional and individual clients, providing investing and wealth advisory solutions, providing financial planning and counseling services, and executing brokerage transactions for wealth management clients. The vast majority of revenues in management and other fees consists of asset-based fees on client assets that we manage. For further information about assets under supervision, see "Assets Under Supervision" below. The fees that we charge vary by asset class, client channel and the types of services provided, and are affected by investment performance, as well as asset inflows and redemptions.

Merrill Wealth Management revenue of $19.1 billion increased nine percent primarily driven by higher asset management fees due to the impact of higher average equity market valuations and positive AUM flows, as well as higher brokerage fees due to increased transactional volume.

comparisons.peer_summary: Asset Management revenue was $10.2 billion, an 11% increase, driven by higher asset management fees due to higher average market levels and strong net inflows, as well as higher performance fees.
comparisons.comparison: Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase both disclose that asset management revenues are significantly driven by asset-based fees responding to market levels and net inflows. Goldman notes its management fees are affected by investment performance and asset inflows, whereas JPMorgan explicitly attributes its 11% revenue increase to higher asset management fees reflecting higher average market levels and strong net inflows. Both firms also identify performance-based returns (incentive fees for GS, performance fees for JPM) as a distinct revenue driver.

sentences.text: • Management and other fees. We receive fees related to managing assets for institutional and individual clients, providing investing and wealth advisory solutions, providing financial planning and counseling services, and executing brokerage transactions for wealth management clients. The vast majority of revenues in management and other fees consists of asset-based fees on client assets that we manage. For further information about assets under supervision, see "Assets Under Supervision" below. The fees that we charge vary by asset class, client channel and the types of services provided, and are affected by investment performance, as well as asset inflows and redemptions.

• Incentive fees. In certain circumstances, we also receive incentive fees based on a percentage of a fund's or a separately managed account's return, or when the return exceeds a specified benchmark or other performance targets. Such fees include overrides, which consist of the increased share of the income and gains derived primarily from our private equity and credit funds when the return on a fund's investments over the life of the fund exceeds certain threshold returns.
